---
title: "Authoring and support"
---

## Start with a native export

Use a Moodle STACK export whose root is `<quiz>` and whose questions use `<question type="stack">`. Keep the normal question, input, PRT, deployed-seed, and qtest elements. Point a `stack-question` block at its XML path and exact `<name><text>…</text></name>`. The filter embeds a selected question and precomputes the requested variants when Quarto renders. The original XML remains the source of truth and can be imported back into Moodle.

```{.stack-question}
#| file: ../questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| seed: 17
#| variants: 3
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
```

The learner submits in two steps: **Validate answers** parses the current fields and displays the expression form (for example, `x+x` rather than a simplified `2*x`), then **Check answer** grades that validated response. Editing any field invalidates the preview, so the learner must validate again. This explicit check mirrors the question input verification setting and helps learners catch syntax errors before grading. The polynomial example sets `<insertstars>1</insertstars>`, so `x**2+8x+15` previews as one sum and receives full credit in its first variant.

Below a rendered question, **Show source** reveals its authored Quarto fenced block and **Show STACK source** reveals the original XML file contents. Both panels start closed; they are available for inspecting and copying a working example.

The options are `file` and `question` (required), `seed` (signed integer, default 1), `variants` (1–20, default 1), `review` (`true` or `false`, default false), and `diagnostics` (`true` or `false`, default false). `feedback: true` opts a card into the [shared AI Feedback extension](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback); cards without it need no AI dependency. Install both extensions in the same project. `context: auto` (default) uses nearby visible prose; `context: none` omits it; `context: id1,id2` includes tagged blocks such as `::: {#id1 .ai-context}` (`.ai-feedback-context` and `.math-exercise-context` are shared aliases). `feedback-language` sets the explanation language (default document `lang`). `feedback-policy` selects an existing named policy from `ai-feedback.policy-files` or page policy files. A stable `label` targets exercise-specific policy settings; otherwise the card ID is used. The shared mathematics policy (`math-exercise`) supplies the default hints and is also the YAML integration namespace for STACK cards. A fixed seed reproduces a variant within this implementation. It does not promise the same pseudo-random sequence as Moodle's Maxima backend.

Feedback uses a learner's current answer, visible question text and selected context. A preceding matching **Check answer** can contribute minimal result status, finite score; XML, source panels, teacher answers, qtests, grader configuration, grader feedback messages and answer notes are excluded. It never grades a response or replaces **Validate answers** and **Check answer**. The shared settings panel lets a learner choose copy-prompt mode or configure their own compatible provider; no API key is placed in the page. The same [nested YAML policy layers](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback/blob/main/docs/feedback-policies.md) are inherited across integrations, using `math-exercise` for STACK's mathematics policy namespace.

## What the adapter checks

| Supported here | Scope |
|---|---|
| Source | Moodle STACK XML `<quiz>` with named STACK questions; category and description entries are skipped. |
| Inputs | Scalar algebraic and numerical text answers, with strict syntax and `<insertstars>0</insertstars>` or `<insertstars>1</insertstars>`. Mode 0 requires `*`; mode 1 also accepts adjacent `2x`, `2(x+1)`, `(x+1)(x-1)`, and `(x+1)x`. Both keep `xy` as one symbol; whitespace alone never means multiplication. Other insertstars modes fail at import. |
| Variables | A small, safely parsed Maxima-like assignment and arithmetic subset, including `rand(n)` for seeded variants. |
| Tests | `AlgEquiv`, `EqualComAss`, `NumAbsolute`, `NumRelative`, `NumDecPlaces`; blank absolute/relative tolerances default to 0.05, while decimal places require an explicit count from 1 to 50. See the README for the expression whitelist. |
| PRTs | Acyclic node graphs with `=`, `+`, and `−` score operations, weighted response trees, branch feedback and notes. |
| Author tests | Native `<qtest>` inputs and expected PRT score, penalty, and answer note. |

This is a deliberately limited evaluator, not a replacement for Moodle STACK or its Maxima CAS. `questionsimplify=0` is accepted when any `EqualComAss` teacher form can be preserved after freezing author variables; otherwise the build rejects it. `EqualComAss` requires a direct input name in `sans` to preserve the student’s written form. Build-time validation rejects unsupported author features rather than silently grading them differently. Symbolic equivalence uses SymPy transformations rather than randomized substitution. Decimal-place grading reads the literal answer so a trailing zero is meaningful. The review interface and qtests help an author inspect parity, but they do not establish complete parity with all STACK configurations.

## Validate and publish

For an extension-only installation, install `sympy==1.13.3` in the Python environment used by Quarto. Run `python -m stack_sympy.cli test --file questions/polynomial-expansion.xml` after placing `_extensions/stack-sympy` on `PYTHONPATH`, then render with `quarto render`. Serve the `_site` directory through an HTTP server, including locally: `python -m http.server --directory _site 8000`. Browser grading loads Pyodide and SymPy; its first use downloads runtime packages, so it needs network access. Review the generated question and run its qtests before publishing any assessment. If a source uses features outside the supported subset, `#| diagnostics: true` displays the location of a build error in the page during authoring; remove it for production so unsupported questions fail the render.
